conversation_history.content: Hi, I am Aryan, a final year CS student. I built InterviewMate, an AI interview prep platform using Node and MongoDB.

Hi Aryan, it’s great to meet you. Building an AI-driven platform like InterviewMate sounds like a solid project that aligns well with our stack. Let’s dive straight into the technical side. How did you structure your Node.js application to handle concurrent interview sessions, and what specific challenges did you face with MongoDB during high-load scenarios?
I used Express with async handlers and stored sessions in MongoDB with indexes on sessionId. Under load I hit connection pool exhaustion, so I tuned poolSize and added Redis caching for hot reads.

That’s a practical approach to managing connection limits and read latency. Since you mentioned using Redis for caching, how did you handle cache invalidation to ensure data consistency between MongoDB and Redis when session data was updated?
I used write-through caching with short TTLs and explicit invalidation on session update, plus versioned keys to avoid stale reads.
That’s a robust strategy for maintaining data consistency. Given your experience with REST APIs, how do you ensure your API endpoints remain secure and performant when handling sensitive user data?

projects.title: ClinicalLens – RAG Pipeline for Pharmaceutical Documents
points: Built a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) application for pharmaceutical document question answering using Gemini and ChromaDB.
Implemented document chunking, embedding generation, vector indexing, retrieval, and response generation as an end-to-end AI pipeline.
Developed a FastAPI backend and Streamlit interface to expose the retrieval and generation workflow through a user-facing application.
Designed the workflow to connect unstructured documents with semantic retrieval and AI-generated responses, demonstrating practical application of LLM-based systems.

projects.title: Automated REST API Testing & CI/CD Pipeline
projects.tech: FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Pytest, Docker, GitHub Actions, Postman, Newman
points: Built a REST API using FastAPI and PostgreSQL with CRUD operations, authentication, and pagination.
Developed 44 automated unit and integration tests using Pytest, achieving 97% code coverage across API functionality.
Created Postman/Newman contract tests to validate response schemas and edge cases including invalid authentication, missing fields, and 404 responses.
Implemented a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline executing linting, automated testing, and Docker builds on every code push.

projects.title: Deepfake Buster – AI Video Forensics Platform
projects.tech: Python, Flask, TensorFlow, OpenCV, XceptionNet, MesoNet, SVM
points: Developed an AI-powered video forensics platform to detect manipulated videos using XceptionNet, MesoNet, and Support Vector Machine models.
Built preprocessing and inference pipelines covering frame extraction, face detection, normalization, and model evaluation using OpenCV and TensorFlow.
Developed Flask backend APIs, automated forensic PDF reporting, and an interactive workflow for video upload and result visualization.
Benchmarked three models on the UADFV dataset, achieving 82% accuracy with XceptionNet, 77% with SVM, and 76% with MesoNet.
Integrated Supabase for authentication, report storage, and user management.
